transport: gloo over shared memory, one host
grid_construction: log-spaced backbone rounded to 4-byte words, NOT restricted to powers of two, plus oversampling in four named regions

oversampled_regions.name: latency_to_bandwidth
oversampled_regions.why: where the latency floor gives way to a bandwidth slope

oversampled_regions.name: cache_peak
oversampled_regions.why: where effective bandwidth peaked in the previous campaign, consistent with the buffer still fitting in cache

oversampled_regions.name: peak_decline
oversampled_regions.why: where bandwidth fell again past the peak

oversampled_regions.name: prior_breakpoints
oversampled_regions.why: where the earlier two-segment fits placed their breakpoints

pass_purpose: two independent passes so the bandwidth peak's location, magnitude and regime ordering can be compared; a peak seen once is not a property of the transport
cross_validation: stratified k-fold over message size, folds assigned round-robin within each regime so no fold can be missing a regime

acceptance.why_not_pooled: a pooled median lets one useless regime hide behind three good ones, which is how a model 35% wrong in the medium tier was previously accepted

a_regime_is_covered_when: it was measured with at least min_points_per_regime valid points
held-out validation graded the model in that regime
the regime's cross-validated error is within the threshold
measurement noise in that regime is within max_noise_cv

subsystem_readiness: conjunctive: every required group covered, every required regime covered, accepted models only, held-out validation present in every cell. There is no arithmetic that trades a covered group against a missing one.
transferability: NOTHING measured here is a value for NVLink or InfiniBand. This is gloo over shared memory on one host. What the campaign can establish is methodology readiness -- that the grid, the estimators, the selection rule and the coverage criteria work -- not fabric parameters for an A100 node.
